claims.statement: The EU battery-passport obligation begins on 18 February 2027 for EV batteries placed on the market or put into service and includes individual-battery information; it does not by itself retroactively furnish every older used EV with a trusted independent assessment.
UN GTR No. 22 creates standardised in-vehicle battery durability metrics and a health-monitor framework, validating the technical category while increasing future standardisation.

Independent operators have EU rights to standardised, non-discriminatory access to OBD and repair information, and users have Data Act rights to readily available connected-product data, but those rights do not require a vehicle to generate every desired battery variable.
The direct Polish market price for a CARA Approved certificate is 400 PLN, while European consumer alternatives advertise EUR 79 and EUR 99 certificates.
DEKRA already markets an independent 15-minute test, and Recurrent gives supported owners a free longitudinal report using data from more than 30,000 connected EVs.
Robust cross-model state-of-health estimation remains technically difficult because large-scale high-quality field data are limited and field behaviour differs from laboratory data.
Poland had about 121,259 passenger BEVs at the end of 2025, which supports a growing local test market but makes 30,000 annual domestic tests a high penetration assumption.

Geotab's 22,700-vehicle analysis reports modern batteries are robust on average while preserving meaningful model and operating-condition variation; urgency is therefore transaction-specific, not universal.
No reviewed source establishes dealer conversion, incremental resale value, or lower warranty losses from a new Polish certificate relative to incumbent certificates.

contrary_evidence: The category has direct, credible incumbents with recognised methods and published prices at or below the proposed retail range.
A free longitudinal report is available in supported markets, and built-in or regulatory data availability is improving.
Average fleet degradation is modest, so many ordinary used EVs may not create enough perceived risk to trigger a paid test.
The domestic fleet is growing quickly but is still too small to assume 30,000 paid tests annually without unusually high attachment to transactions.
